A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Similar/MCTS-P/Triple-M research and SRM benchmark. Both contain readable main text and Appendices A–F, with corresponding equations, algorithms, figures, and tables supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original preference-alignment accuracies, agent success rates, inference-scaling results, ablations, and human acceptance measurements in Tables 1–6 and Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies, including the appendix analyses, and revises reported results in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 reverses the sign factor in the stated Helpfulness computation from (1 - 2r_i) to (2r_i - 1). This is a localized scoring-rule revision; the MCTS-P pipeline, regression and gating architecture, and training losses remain unchanged. Similar-3M becoming Similar-TM is a rename.

E1.justification: Both versions use WebArena, VisualWebArena, Android World, and OSWorld to construct SRM and retain the same preference-evaluation and agent-training/inference tasks. Appendix examples and benchmark coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods and agents. GPT-4o, GPT-4-Turbo, and InternVL-2.5 already appear in v1 Table 1; their explicit listing in v2 Section 5.1 adds documentation, not comparators. Similar-3M and Similar-TM denote the same model variant.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 revises the reported evaluation prompt: actions 1/2 become X/Y, but the instructions now request Y when X is better and X when Y is better. Some dimension-specific guidance is also removed. These are reported prompt changes; the PDFs do not establish rerunning experiments. Splits, dataset sizes, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The dimensional ablations in Tables 4 and 6, inference-scaling and correlation analyses in Figure 6, human acceptance study in Table 5, and appendix cases are retained. Expanded annotation documentation does not introduce a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point estimates and the same correlation analysis without adding run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Newly disclosed annotation staffing does not constitute repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 extensively revises scores and rankings: reported Avg values change from 10.3 to 42.9 for Qwen2-VL, 39.5 to 51.4 for GPT-4o, and 60.8 to 61.2 for Similar-3M/TM-Llama. In Table 2, OS-Atlas with Llama-based Similar-RL changes WebArena SR from 27.0 to 27.4, and Similar-3M/TM from 37.3 to 35.6. These are revised reported results, not established same-protocol gains. Tables 3–6 and Figure 6 retain their numerical findings.

T1.justification: The Helpfulness formula's sign correction in Section 3.1 aligns it with the existing positive-for-success interpretation. However, Appendix Algorithm 2 retains the old (1 - 2r_i) factor, leaving an inconsistency. Other definitions and mathematical objectives remain unchanged; no new proof or theorem is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: five-dimensional process rewards, automated MCTS-P annotation, Triple-M synergy, the SRM benchmark, and benefits for agent training and inference. Updated numerical gains revise supporting results without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 removes the assertion that an efficient action necessarily is correct. Appendix C newly explains unequal audit sample sizes through the binary nature of Task Relevance and Coherence scores. The principal interpretations of ablations and limitations concerning annotation quality and untested domains remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents commercial annotators, three training cycles, validation thresholds above 95%, three annotators and three checkers per test sample, and a final accuracy requirement above 99%. It also explains trajectory diversity generation, specifies comparator versions, and changes the declared code location from Similar-v1 to antgroup/Similar. These disclosures do not establish changes to the underlying implementation or annotation process.

R1.justification: v2 adds background citations including the GVA survey, OmniBench, and multimodal CoT reward benchmarking, plus an MLLM background paragraph in Appendix B. It replaces the GPT-4 technical-report citation with the GPT-4o system card. The substantive positioning against earlier reward-model approaches remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes Similar-TM naming, rewrites selected method and experimental explanations, corrects appendix action tags, adds acknowledgments, and trims prompts and the impact statement. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 gain shaded model rows, Figure 6(a)'s legend adopts the renamed model, and captions, running headers, and algorithm placement change. The same six figures and seven tables remain; Figure 6(a)'s plotted curves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves annotation transparency and corrects the main-text Helpfulness sign. However, the appendix retains the conflicting formula, the revised evaluation prompt introduces unexplained opposite-label outputs, and substantial Table 1 revisions are not connected to an explained experimental change. The PDFs do not establish whether these inconsistencies are merely documentary or affected evaluation. Consequently, the documentation gains and uncertainty about the revised evidence do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
